resources.string: Resizable stock watchlist with dense two-column rows, transparent backgrounds, multiline cards and gradient intraday charts.

Enter tickers or supported asset names, separated by commas or new lines. Tap a stock on the widget for its full name, trend chart and related news; long-press remains a launcher control. Your last-used watchlist and groups are remembered after removing the widget. New or unverified tickers must be verified online before saving.
AAPL, MSFT, gold, crude oil, BND
Enter valid tickers or supported asset names, not URLs. Put group headings on separate lines, such as [Commodities], with at least one ticker under each heading.
Dense: larger text, price and % change
Cards: ticker, company, price and daily change
Show 1-day charts with gradient fill below each card
Two columns when there is enough width

Use 80 to 180 percent of the normal text size for this layout. Applies immediately to existing widgets, including prices and changes. Larger text may use one column or require a wider widget. The default is 100 percent.

For a dense two-column list, choose Dense, enable Two columns, and hide currency labels. Green/red changes compare with the previous trading close, not the first chart point. Dense mode marks cached quotes with *. On transparent backgrounds, choose light or dark text to suit your wallpaper.
Use a name of 1 to 40 characters, without square brackets or line breaks.

Add group inserts a [Heading] after the current line. Put stocks beneath it; move whole sections to reorder groups. A trailing minus, such as [Commodities-], adds a line beside the group name on the same row and is hidden from the displayed heading. This also works with Headings only. Place the cursor in a group before adding an instrument. Commodity names refer to futures, not spot prices. Bonds here are ETFs or Treasury futures, not individual bonds or yields. Prefix a literal ticker with $ to bypass an asset alias (for example $CORN for the ETF).
Find stocks, funds, indices or commodities

Typing filters built-in shortcuts locally. Tap Search Yahoo or the keyboard search key to find stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, indices, currencies and other instruments covered by Yahoo. Only your search text is sent to Yahoo. Select a result to add it to the current group; quotes are verified before saving. Mutual funds may update only once daily.

For existing widgets, display options and refresh interval save immediately, even when you leave with Back. Ticker and group-content edits still require Verify and save. New widgets require verification before any settings are saved.
Tickers verified. Confirm the instruments to save.
Could not verify %1$s. Check the ticker and your connection, or retry if the provider is unavailable. Ticker and group-content edits have not been saved.

Data: Yahoo Finance (unofficial, no account or API key). Online lookup sends the search text you submit; verification sends chosen ticker symbols. Saving enables automatic quote requests. Yahoo sees your IP address. Group names, messages, contacts, device location and browser sessions are not added to these requests.\n\nQuotes may be delayed or unavailable, and Android may delay background refresh. Charts show the latest trading session returned by Yahoo, at 5-minute intervals; they are not live feeds. Mutual funds may only update once daily. Cached quotes are labeled when a refresh fails or is overdue. Manual refresh is limited to once per minute per symbol. No holdings, alerts or trading features.
